title: The Tryouts of Cedar Falls
premise: Ada Nakamura has spent seventeen years as the quiet kid behind the counter of his family's bakery, kneading loneliness into sourdough and counting down to graduation. When he finds his late grandmother's recipe box, he discovers cards that aren't recipes at all but instructions for the Tryouts of Cedar Falls—a generations-old rite where townsfolk bake their truest selves into bread, and the town's founding covenant is renewed each spring. This year's Tryouts have been quietly cancelled by a developer-backed council eager to erase the town's odd history, and Ada learns his grandmother was the last Keeper of the box. As prom approaches and the bakery faces foreclosure, Ada must gather a ragtag found family of misfits, learn to bake feelings he'd rather hide, and stage an unsanctioned Tryout that forces the whole town to taste the truth—ending with Ada claiming his place as the new Keeper and choosing Cedar Falls not because he's trapped, but because it's his.
about_author: Beatrix Coldharbour is the pen name of a former small-town baker who once won a county fair ribbon for a grief loaf nobody asked her to make. She writes stories about kids who discover magic hiding in ordinary kitchens.

chapters.title: Proofing Period
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Opening on a gray March morning at Nakamura Bakery, Ada counts 94 days until graduation while mechanically shaping loaves. A customer cries over his cinnamon rolls and he pretends not to notice that his bread does something to people. Establishes his invisibility strategy and exhaustion. Emotional beat: numb resignation masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Box Under the Flour Shelf
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cleaning out grandma Sanae's old station in the back room, Ada finds her recipe box—and inside, cards written in her hand that read like rituals: 'Fold in one honest memory. Let rise under a full moon.' The final card names him: 'For my Ada, when he stops hiding.' Emotional beat: startled curiosity cracking open grief.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days of Nothing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV at school. We meet his only friend Priya (debate-team cynic) and crush-object Theo, plus the social geography Ada navigates by being forgettable. News breaks: the Spring Festival—the town's oldest tradition—is cancelled this year, replaced by a 'Cedar Falls Futures Expo' sponsored by the Hollis Development Group. Emotional beat: quiet injustice Ada almost ignores.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kneaded
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Testing one of the strange cards half-jokingly, Ada bakes a loaf with a written memory folded into the dough. His father eats a slice and, for the first time since mom left, talks about her—then doesn't remember why. Ada realizes the cards work, and that grandma's 'recipes' shaped the whole town's heart. Emotional beat: awe tangled with fear.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada POV with grandma Sanae's journal entries from 1974. Ada discovers she was the last 'Keeper' of the Tryouts of Cedar Falls—a hidden spring rite where residents bake their truest selves and the town renews its founding covenant. Her last entry: 'The box chooses the next Keeper. I pray it isn't Ada; I pray it is.' Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and invitation.

chapters.title: Misfits and Measuring Cups
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada accidentally reveals the magic to Priya when her 'apology loaf' for her estranged sister works too well. Instead of freaking out, Priya recruits him: if the Tryouts are what kept Cedar Falls weird and alive, cancelling them is how Hollis plans to flatten the town's soul. They need a team. Emotional beat: first spark of purpose.

chapters.title: Theo Orders Rye
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Theo starts showing up daily, ordering things he never eats, clearly using the bakery to escape something at home. A shared closing shift turns into real conversation, and Ada nearly tells him everything. Meanwhile Dad announces the bakery may not survive past June. Emotional beat: longing and the terror of being seen.

chapters.title: The Council of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya infiltrates a town council meeting and learns the festival cancellation was engineered by councilwoman Marsh, whose family once tried and failed a Tryout decades ago. The covenant, Marsh believes, is superstition that keeps Cedar Falls poor and stuck. Emotional beat: righteous anger meeting uncomfortable nuance—Marsh isn't wrong about everything.

chapters.title: A Loaf of Almosts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada attempts the hardest card: baking his own truth. What comes out is a dense, bitter brick—he can't name what he actually feels or wants. He burns it in the alley and lies to Priya about progress. Emotional beat: self-deception curdling; the magic demands honesty he doesn't have yet.

chapters.title: Flour on His Hands, Prom on His Mind
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, hiding his family's eviction notice, asks Ada to prom in the world's most deniable way. Ada says yes before his invisibility instinct can veto it. That night he tries another recipe-card experiment and hears, faintly, the oven humming like it's answering him. Emotional beat: giddy hope undercut by dread.

chapters.title: The Old Guard
chapters.summary: Ada and Priya's alternating POV. Following ledger clues, they find three elderly Keepers-in-hiding: Mr. Okafor the locksmith, widow Ruth Alvarez, and gruff diner owner Sal. They confirm the Tryouts are real, warn that an unlicensed Tryout without a Keeper 'takes more than it gives,' and refuse to help—until Ruth tastes Ada's bread and goes silent. 'You're hers,' she says. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming.

chapters.title: Rising Trouble
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Training montage of sorts: the elders teach Ada the rules—consent, honesty, a Keeper to anchor the circle—but the bakery gets a health inspection clearly tipped off by Marsh, and Dad, humiliated, forbids Ada's 'experiments.' Ada hides the box at Priya's. Emotional beat: pressure compressing from every side.

chapters.title: Half-Baked Plans
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew drafts a plan: hold the Tryout on prom night inside the closed expo hall, when the whole town will be in one building. It's reckless, possibly dangerous, definitely illegal. Theo commits fully; Ada wavers, terrified the Tryout will expose him—his grief, his queerness, his wanting to leave. Emotional beat: fear of exposure versus hunger for belonging.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada discovers a card in the box in different handwriting—his mother's. She wasn't just a woman who left; she refused a Tryout, rejected the covenant, and walked away from the Keeper line. Ada spirals: is he destined to abandon Cedar Falls too? Fight with Dad; the bakery feels smaller than ever. Emotional beat: identity crisis deepening.

chapters.title: Sourdough Confessions
chapters.summary: Dad's POV. Hiro Nakamura, unable to sleep, finds Ada's practice loaves and recognizes his mother's technique in them. He bakes beside his son in silence, then finally speaks about Ada's mother—not as abandonment but as a woman suffocated by a town that baked her feelings for her without consent. Father and son reach an uneasy truce. Emotional beat: generational wound partially aired.

chapters.title: Marsh's Counter-Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Councilwoman Marsh corners Ada at the bakery, revealing she knows exactly what he's found. Her offer: hand over the box, let the covenant die peacefully, and Hollis will save the bakery with a franchise deal. She shows him her own failed Tryout card from 1989—her truth was 'I want to matter,' and the town laughed. Emotional beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Priya, Theo, Ruth). Prom-eve chaos: dresses, corsages, smuggled ovens, Sal's diner kitchen turned command center. Theo gives Ada his grandmother's ring as a promise; Priya reconciles with her sister via one last test loaf. But Ruth warns: a Tryout held in fear instead of love can hollow people out. Ada must decide what he's really offering the town. Emotional beat: tender anticipation over live wires.

chapters.title: Prom, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Mid-prom, Marsh cuts the power and locks the expo hall, planning to hold everyone until the covenant deadline passes at midnight. Ada, in front of everyone he's spent years hiding from, steps onto the stage and tells the truth: about the bread, the box, the Tryouts, himself. Some laugh. Some don't. Emotional beat: the invisibility strategy dies spectacularly.

chapters.title: The Tryout of Cedar Falls
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. By candlelight and phone flashlights, Ada anchors an improvised Tryout: dozens of townspeople bake their truths—grief, shame, hope, Marsh's own 'I want to matter' among them. The hall fills with the smell of forty honest loaves, and the covenant renews itself as the building literally warms. Marsh, tasting her own old truth offered back kindly, stands down. Emotional beat: cathartic communal release.

chapters.title: Crust and Crumb
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, exhausted dawn after. Consequences arrive gently: the council can't un-cancel a tradition the whole town witnessed; Hollis withdraws; the bakery's fate reverses on a wave of customers wanting 'the honest bread.' Ada formally accepts the Keeper role from Ruth, Okafor, and Sal. Theo and Ada have their actual first kiss amid flour dust. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging.

chapters.title: Graduation Day, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ninety-four days later: graduation. Ada walks the stage no longer invisible—known, loved, occasionally embarrassed by both. He's deferred college one year to run the bakery and train as Keeper, with dad as partner and the found family as staff. He adds his first card to the box in his own handwriting. Emotional beat: choosing home as freedom, not sentence.

chapters.title: For Whoever Stops Hiding Next
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ada's POV, one year on. Spring Tryouts are now official again, held openly in the town square. A shy new kid lingers at the bakery counter, and Ada slides them a roll that tastes like courage, watching for the flicker of recognition. The final image: the recipe box, open, waiting, full of blank cards. Emotional beat: legacy passed forward with open hands.
